answer: A verifiable delay function protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by forcing agents to solve sequential cryptographic proofs to join network consensus. Whether logging timber logistics or recording ocean tide telemetry, an agent must finalize time-locked proofs before each dawn epoch begins. An attacker incurs the verifiable, scarce cost of dedicated single-core processing time per identity. However, this continuous computation wastes electrical energy and penalizes lightweight edge devices.
